title: Constraining Participation: Affordances of Feedback Features in Interfaces to Large Language Models
reasoning: The paper examines the socio-technical affordances of feedback interfaces (like ChatGPT's thumbs-up/down) and how they shape user participation in the alignment process. While it discusses 'ethical concerns' and 'alignment' as categories of feedback users might want to provide, the paper itself is a study of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) and participatory design, not an evaluation or benchmark of moral, ethical, or religious content/systems.
